text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for high blood pressure (hypertension) include lifestyle changes, prescription medications, and combination therapies tailored to your specific blood pressure stage and cardiovascular risk.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, prescription medications, and combination therapies tailored to your specific blood pressure stage and cardiovascular risk

text_blocks.snippet: Lifestyle changes form the foundation of managing and preventing high blood pressure:
When lifestyle changes are not enough—or immediately for Stage 2 hypertension (140/90 mmHg or higher)—doctors prescribe one or more first-line drug classes:
Depending on underlying health conditions (such as heart failure, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease), your doctor may prescribe:

Many people require two or more blood pressure medications to reach their target goal (typically under 130/80 mmHg). Doctors often use single-pill combinations (combining two classes like an ARB and a CCB or diuretic) to improve convenience, lower side effects, and help control blood pressure faster.
You can read more clinical details on the Mayo Clinic Diagnosis & Treatment Guide or review medication classes via the American Heart Association.
